I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years, and I know every corner of this land. It is just my husband and me at home now—our children work in the city—so I cannot afford wasteful practices. I have a well, which means I can irrigate when the sky refuses to rain, but pumping costs electricity, so I water only when the crops truly need it.

My winter wheat is already in the ground; I sowed it last October after rotary tillage with improved seed I refreshed from the seed shop two years ago. For the wheat, I will topdress urea at green-up and again at jointing, and I will run the well three times: at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray pesticides three times—herbicide once early, then insecticide and fungicide later—to keep aphids and powdery mildew under control. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After wheat harvest in early June, the race begins. I will buy hybrid maize seed from the agricultural shop—Nongda or something similar—and sow it immediately without plowing. No-tillage saves diesel, keeps the soil moisture, and lets me plant fast before the summer heat sets in. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and one more round of urea at the big trumpet stage. The maize gets two irrigations, at jointing and filling, and I spray herbicide and insecticide three times total. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

I do not throw fertilizer around like I did 20 years ago; prices are too high, and my experience tells me that restraint pays off.
